Symbol.name: alias
Symbol.Description: Define an alias. Bash builtin. With no arguments or with -p, prints the aliases; name=value defines an alias.

Symbol.name: bg
Symbol.Description: Resume jobs in the background. Bash builtin. Resumes each suspended job in the background; with no job specification, uses the current job.

Symbol.name: bind
Symbol.Description: Manage Readline key bindings. Bash builtin. Displays or changes Readline key bindings, macros and variables.

Symbol.name: break
Symbol.Description: Exit a loop. Bash builtin. Exits the innermost for, while, until or select loop; an optional count exits that many enclosing loops.

Symbol.name: builtin
Symbol.Description: Run a shell builtin directly. Bash builtin. Runs the named builtin, bypassing a shell function with the same name.

Symbol.name: caller
Symbol.Description: Show the call stack. Bash builtin. Prints the line number, function name and source file of a subroutine call.

Symbol.name: cd
Symbol.Description: Change the working directory. Bash builtin. Changes the current directory; with no argument, uses HOME, and '-' returns to OLDPWD.

Symbol.name: command
Symbol.Summary: Run a command without function lookup
Symbol.Description: Run a command without function lookup. Bash builtin. Runs a command while ignoring shell functions with the same name; -v or -V describes how the name would be resolved.

Symbol.name: compgen
Symbol.Description: Generate completion matches. Bash builtin. Generates possible completions for a word according to the selected completion action.

Symbol.name: complete
Symbol.Description: Configure programmable completion. Bash builtin. Registers or displays completion specifications for commands.

Symbol.name: compopt
Symbol.Description: Change completion options. Bash builtin. Modifies the options of the completion specification currently being executed.

Symbol.name: continue
Symbol.Description: Resume a loop. Bash builtin. Resumes the next iteration of an enclosing for, while, until or select loop; an optional count selects an outer loop.

Symbol.name: declare
Symbol.Description: Declare a variable. Bash builtin. Declares variables, sets attributes such as -i, -r, -x or -a, and displays existing values with -p.

Symbol.name: dirs
Symbol.Description: Show the directory stack. Bash builtin. Displays the directory stack maintained by pushd and popd.

Symbol.name: disown
Symbol.Summary: Remove jobs from the job table
Symbol.Description: Remove jobs from the job table. Bash builtin. Removes jobs from the active job table or marks them so SIGHUP is not sent.

Symbol.name: echo
Symbol.Summary: Write the arguments and a newline
Symbol.Description: Write the arguments and a newline. Bash builtin. Writes its arguments separated by spaces; -n suppresses the newline and -e enables backslash escapes.

Symbol.name: enable
Symbol.Description: Enable or disable builtins. Bash builtin. Enables or disables shell builtins, and can load a builtin from a shared object.

Symbol.name: eval
Symbol.Description: Evaluate text as a command. Bash builtin. Concatenates its arguments and executes the result in the current shell.

Symbol.name: exec
Symbol.Summary: Replace the shell with a command
Symbol.Description: Replace the shell with a command. Bash builtin. Replaces the shell process with the named command; without a command, applies redirections to the current shell.

Symbol.name: exit
Symbol.Description: Leave the shell. Bash builtin. Exits the shell with the given status, or with the status of the last command.

Symbol.name: export
Symbol.Summary: Mark a variable for the environment
Symbol.Description: Mark a variable for the environment. Bash builtin. Exports variables to subsequent commands; -n removes the export attribute and -f applies to functions.

Symbol.name: false
Symbol.Description: Return a failure status. Bash builtin. Does nothing and returns a non-zero status.

Symbol.name: fc
Symbol.Description: Edit and re-run history commands. Bash builtin. Lists, edits or re-executes commands from the history list.

Symbol.name: fg
Symbol.Summary: Resume a job in the foreground
Symbol.Description: Resume a job in the foreground. Bash builtin. Resumes the selected job in the foreground and makes it the current job.

Symbol.name: getopts
Symbol.Description: Parse command-line options. Bash builtin. Parses positional parameters as options, storing the option in name and its argument in OPTARG.

Symbol.name: hash
Symbol.Description: Manage the command hash table. Bash builtin. Remembers command paths to avoid repeated PATH searches; -r forgets them.

Symbol.name: help
Symbol.Description: Show help for builtins. Bash builtin. Displays usage and documentation for shell builtins and compound commands.

Symbol.name: history
Symbol.Description: Manage the command history. Bash builtin. Displays, searches, reads or writes the command history list.

Symbol.name: jobs
Symbol.Description: List or control jobs. Bash builtin. Lists active jobs and their status; -l adds process IDs.

Symbol.name: kill
Symbol.Description: Send a signal to processes. Bash builtin. Sends a signal to the named processes or jobs; -l lists signal names.

Symbol.name: let
Symbol.Description: Arithmetic evaluation. Bash builtin. Evaluates each expression as shell arithmetic; the status is zero when the last value is non-zero.

Symbol.name: local
Symbol.Summary: Declare a local variable in a function
Symbol.Description: Declare a local variable in a function. Bash builtin. Creates variables local to the enclosing shell function; the options are those of declare.

Symbol.name: logout
Symbol.Description: Leave a login shell. Bash builtin. Exits a login shell with the given status.

Symbol.name: mapfile
Symbol.Description: Read lines into an array. Bash builtin. Reads lines from standard input or a file descriptor into an indexed array; readarray is a synonym.

Symbol.name: popd
Symbol.Summary: Remove a directory from the stack
Symbol.Description: Remove a directory from the stack. Bash builtin. Removes entries from the directory stack and changes to the new top directory.

Symbol.name: printf
Symbol.Description: Formatted output. Bash builtin. Writes formatted arguments; -v stores the result in a variable instead of printing it.

Symbol.name: pushd
Symbol.Summary: Add or rotate the directory stack
Symbol.Description: Add or rotate the directory stack. Bash builtin. Adds a directory to the stack or rotates it, then changes to the new top directory.

Symbol.name: pwd
Symbol.Description: Print the working directory. Bash builtin. Prints the absolute pathname of the current directory; -P resolves symbolic links.

Symbol.name: read
Symbol.Summary: Read a line into a variable
Symbol.Description: Read a line into a variable. Bash builtin. Reads a line from standard input and splits it into variables using IFS.

Symbol.name: readarray
Symbol.Description: Read lines into an array. Bash builtin. A synonym for mapfile.

Symbol.name: readonly
Symbol.Description: Mark variables as read-only. Bash builtin. Prevents later assignment or unset of the named variables or functions.

Symbol.name: return
Symbol.Description: Return from a function. Bash builtin. Stops the current function or sourced script and returns the given status.

Symbol.name: set
Symbol.Summary: Set shell options or positional parameters
Symbol.Description: Set shell options or positional parameters. Bash builtin. Sets shell options, positional parameters and displays variables.

Symbol.name: shift
Symbol.Description: Drop positional parameters. Bash builtin. Renames positional parameters n+1 and later to $1 and later, dropping the first n.

Symbol.name: shopt
Symbol.Description: Set shell options. Bash builtin. Enables, disables or lists the Bash-specific shell options.

Symbol.name: source
Symbol.Summary: Run a file in the current shell
Symbol.Description: Run a file in the current shell. Bash builtin. Reads and executes a file in the current shell; a synonym for '.'.

Symbol.name: suspend
Symbol.Description: Suspend the shell. Bash builtin. Suspends the shell until it receives SIGCONT; -f forces suspension of a login shell.

Symbol.name: test
Symbol.Description: Evaluate a condition. Bash builtin. Evaluates a conditional expression and returns zero for true or one for false; '[' is the same command.

Symbol.name: times
Symbol.Summary: Print shell and child CPU times
Symbol.Description: Print shell and child CPU times. Bash builtin. Prints the user and system time used by the shell and its children.

Symbol.name: trap
Symbol.Description: Handle a signal. Bash builtin. Sets or displays commands to run when a signal, EXIT, DEBUG, RETURN or ERR event occurs.

Last argument or command path. Bash variable. Expands to the last argument of the previous command and to the path of the running command.
